title: What licensing, vetting and safeguarding training does ADEK require for school staff in Abu Dhabi?
description: ADEK rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter schools: staff eligibility and licenses, PASS vetting, safeguarding induction, 24 hour reporting, 25 CPD hours.
shortAnswer: Abu Dhabi's Department of Education and Knowledge (ADEK) requires private and charter schools to register and vet every staff member on its PASS portal before engagement, appoint staff who meet the School Staff Eligibility Policy (where a valid license means a UAE Ministry of Education Certified License), give safeguarding training at induction to governors, staff and volunteers, and report suspected maltreatment to ADEK's Child Protection Unit within 24 hours. Staff complete 25 hours of CPD a year.
keyTakeaways: The ADEK School Student Protection Policy makes all staff and volunteers mandated reporters who must report suspected maltreatment directly to ADEK's Child Protection Unit within 24 hours of suspicion.
Each school must appoint a Child Protection Coordinator and a Child Protection Team, report the appointments to ADEK annually, and put them through ADEK mandated training.
The ADEK School Safeguarding Policy requires safeguarding training at induction for the Governing Board, staff and volunteers, covering eight listed topics; compliance was due from February 1, 2026.

The ADEK School Employment Policy requires PASS registration and vetting, including background checks and police clearance, before anyone works in a school, and 25 hours of CPD per staff member per year.
Under the ADEK School Staff Eligibility Policy, a valid license is an MoE Certified License; the MoE Transitional License is accepted only where certified licenses are not yet available.
jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates: Emirate of Abu Dhabi
regulator: Department of Education and Knowledge (ADEK), Abu Dhabi
appliesTo: Private and charter schools in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi regulated by ADEK
Teachers, school leaders, counselors and other staff registered on ADEK PASS
Volunteers and invited visitors, who must be registered and briefed
Governing Boards, principals, Safeguarding Leads, Child Protection Coordinators and Child Protection Teams

sections.heading: Which ADEK policies govern teacher eligibility and safeguarding?

blocks.text: Four ADEK school policies carry the obligations, all published on ADEK's [health, safety and wellbeing](https://www.adek.gov.ae/en/Education-System/Education-Policies/School-Policies-Health-Safety-and-Wellbeing) and [governance and operations](https://www.adek.gov.ae/en/Education-System/Education-Policies/School-Policies-Governance-and-Operations) policy pages. As at November 2026, their published versions and compliance dates are:

blocks.text: The [Student Protection Policy](https://www.adek.gov.ae/-/media/Project/TAMM/ADEK/Policies/School-Policies/Health-safety-and-wellbeing/ADEK_S_Student-Protection-Policy_EN.pdf) states that it "applies to Private and Charter Schools in Abu Dhabi", while circulars issued specifically for charter schools take precedence where they differ. Each policy says failure to comply is subject to legal accountability and the penalties in ADEK's regulations, alongside any penalty under Federal Decree Law No. (31) of 2021 on crimes and penalties.

sections.heading: Do Abu Dhabi teachers need a license, and what counts as a valid one?

blocks.text: Teachers must match an ADEK eligibility profile, and a teaching license is one of the routes into several profiles rather than a single universal requirement. The [School Staff Eligibility Policy](https://www.adek.gov.ae/-/media/Project/TAMM/ADEK/Policies/School-Policies/Governance-and-Operations/ADEK_S_Staff-Eligibility-Policy_EN.pdf) sets minimum qualification and experience profiles for each position. A class teacher with a bachelor's degree in early childhood or primary education qualifies directly, while a graduate in another subject needs a valid teaching license or a teaching diploma, plus experience in some profiles.

The policy defines a valid license as "A 'Certified License' issued by the UAE Ministry of Education (MoE), including an MoE-recognized international license", and adds that the MoE Transitional License "is not considered a valid license but will be accepted where certified licenses are not yet available". For principals and vice principals, a valid educational leadership license can substitute for three years of teaching experience within the required years in education.

Other roles have their own licensing authorities. School counselors were required to apply for a Department of Community Development (DCD) license by August 16, 2024 under DCD Circular OUT/LSI/510/2024, and positions such as bus supervisors, canteen staff, lifeguards and security guards must meet Abu Dhabi Quality and Conformity Council licensing requirements, valid throughout employment.

sections.heading: How are staff vetted before they start in an Abu Dhabi school?

blocks.text: Every staff member must be registered and cleared on ADEK PASS before they start. Section 1 of the [School Employment Policy](https://www.adek.gov.ae/-/media/Project/TAMM/ADEK/Policies/School-Policies/Governance-and-Operations/ADEK_S_Employment-Policy_EN.pdf) requires schools to register all staff on "ADEK PASS (staff licensing portal)" and obtain an appointment letter or work permit before engagement. ADEK vets every candidate and grants approval "only if they pass the latest vetting requirements (e.g., background checks, and police clearance)".

Two points matter for safeguarding. Candidates under investigation for student protection matters will not pass vetting until cleared by the relevant authority, and volunteers and invited visitors must also be registered on ADEK systems with a work permission before engaging with the school.

sections.heading: What safeguarding and student protection training must schools provide?

blocks.text: Schools must train everyone at induction and give designated child protection staff ADEK mandated training. Section 6.1 of the [School Safeguarding Policy](https://www.adek.gov.ae/-/media/Project/TAMM/ADEK/Policies/School-Policies/Health-safety-and-wellbeing/ADEK_S_Safeguarding-Policy_EN_v12.pdf) requires "Safeguarding training at induction, including for the Governing Board, staff, and volunteers". Staff training should cover:

items: identifying signs of maltreatment or other safeguarding issues, and what to do when worried about a student
vigilance for students at risk of harm, including students with additional learning needs
not disregarding behaviors such as banter or practical jokes that can build an unsafe culture
keeping secure, accurate written records and respecting confidentiality under the ADEK School Digital Policy
taking action in emergencies to prevent harm
sharing information only on a need to know basis
support for staff with wellbeing concerns under the ADEK School Staff Wellbeing Policy
the school's security system and security breach protocol

blocks.text: Invited visitors need not be trained but must read and sign the Safeguarding Policy. The school's Safeguarding Committee or Lead must develop the induction and training program and review the policy's effectiveness every year (section 2.2).

The Student Protection Policy adds role specific training in section 5. The Child Protection Coordinator (CPC) and Child Protection Team (CPT) must complete all ADEK mandated student protection and safeguarding training, including an affidavit on ethical case management. All staff must complete any ADEK mandated sessions and "sign off that they have received training and understand their responsibilities". Volunteers need induction and training, and staff who counsel or are in close personal contact with students need continuous training and supervision by the principal.

sections.heading: What must staff do when they suspect a student is being harmed?

blocks.text: They must report it to ADEK's Child Protection Unit (CPU) within 24 hours. Section 3.1 of the Student Protection Policy says school staff, including anyone with regular or temporary contact with students, are mandated by Federal Law No. (3) of 2016 Concerning Child Rights (Wadeema) to report all alleged or suspected maltreatment, inside or outside school, "directly to the ADEK Child Protection Unit (CPU) within 24 hours upon suspicion". Emergencies where a student is in imminent danger go immediately to the police and the principal.

Inside the school, concerns go to the CPC, and the policy says all staff "should be trained on identifying maltreatment" in line with the policy's operational definitions. Schools must appoint a CPC and a CPT of typically three to five members and report these appointments to ADEK annually. Because the reporting duty comes from federal law, the same content applies in Dubai, where the school regulator is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority (see [KHDA child protection training](/regulations/khda-dubai-school-child-protection-training)).

sections.heading: How much CPD must Abu Dhabi school staff complete?

blocks.text: At least 25 hours a year. Section 3.12 of the School Employment Policy requires schools to ensure that "all staff complete 25 hours of CPD annually, including any ADEK-mandated training, at no cost to the staff", citing Federal Decree Law No. (33) of 2021 on labor relations. Staff who need more, under other ADEK policies or their UAE licensing requirements, must be given the opportunity to meet it.

Mandated safeguarding sessions count toward the 25 hours, so a school can plan its annual safeguarding refresh inside the CPD allowance. CPD plans must be discussed in each performance management cycle, and schools must keep accurate documentation of all CPD programs. For the general concept, see [continuing professional development](/glossary/continuing-professional-development); for education employers, see the [higher education and education industry page](/industries/higher-education).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each ADEK policy clause to the roles it names, from Governing Board to CPC, and to the sign off evidence it requires, before safeguarding content is written. Because ADEK versions its policies and sets separate effective and compliance dates, each obligation carries its policy version so changes can be traced to affected courses.

faqs.q: Is the MoE Transitional License accepted by ADEK?
faqs.a: Only as a fallback. The ADEK School Staff Eligibility Policy says the MoE Transitional License is not considered a valid license but will be accepted where certified licenses are not yet available. A valid license is an MoE Certified License, including an MoE recognized international license.

faqs.q: Who must receive safeguarding training at induction in Abu Dhabi schools?
faqs.a: The Governing Board, staff and volunteers, under section 6.1 of the ADEK School Safeguarding Policy. Invited visitors do not need training but must read and sign the school's Safeguarding Policy, and the Student Protection Policy requires visitors to attest that they have read it.

faqs.q: How quickly must suspected maltreatment be reported to ADEK?
faqs.a: Within 24 hours of suspicion, directly to ADEK's Child Protection Unit, under section 3.1 of the School Student Protection Policy. Cases where a student is in imminent danger must be reported immediately to the police and the principal.

faqs.q: Does safeguarding training count toward the 25 CPD hours?
faqs.a: Yes. The ADEK School Employment Policy says the 25 annual CPD hours include any ADEK mandated training and must be provided at no cost to staff. Additional hours required by other policies or licensing must be offered on top.

faqs.q: Can someone under a child protection investigation be hired?
faqs.a: Not until cleared. The ADEK School Employment Policy says candidates under investigation for student protection related matters will not pass PASS vetting until they have received clearance from the respective authority.
